en: products of a place; local produce

examples.ko: 제주도에서 토산품을 몇 개 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I bought a few local products in Jeju.

examples.ko: 이 시장에는 지역 토산품 가게가 많아요.
examples.en: This market has many shops selling local products.

examples.ko: 외국 친구에게 줄 토산품을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a local product to give to my foreign friend.
I picked out some traditional snacks at the local products corner.

examples.ko: 이 도자기는 이 지역의 대표적인 토산품이에요.
examples.en: This pottery is a representative product of this region.

examples.ko: 공항에서 파는 토산품은 값이 조금 비싸요.
examples.en: Local products sold at the airport are a bit expensive.

explain: '기념품'은 어디서든 기념으로 사는 물건이고, '토산품'은 그 지역에서 나거나 만든 물건이라는 점이 달라요. 관광지 가게 간판이나 여행 이야기에서 자주 보여요. 비슷한 '특산품'은 그 지역에서 특히 유명한 산물을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: A '기념품' (souvenir) can be bought anywhere as a keepsake, while a '토산품' is something grown or made in that region. You often see it on shop signs in tourist areas. The similar word '특산품' is used for a product a region is especially famous for.

examples.en: This restaurant is famous for its local traditional food.

examples.ko: 시골 마을에서 토속 신앙의 흔적을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw traces of folk beliefs in a country village.
My grandmother sang in a folk melody.

examples.ko: 토속 분위기가 나는 카페에 가 봤어요.
examples.en: I went to a cafe with a rustic, local atmosphere.

examples.ko: 이 지역의 토속 문화를 소개하는 전시회가 열려요.
examples.en: An exhibition introducing this region's folk culture is being held.

examples.ko: 토속 된장으로 끓인 찌개 맛이 정말 깊어요.
examples.en: The stew made with homemade local soybean paste tastes really deep.

explain: 주로 '토속 음식', '토속 신앙'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙여 써요. '전통'이 오래 이어진 것 전반이라면, '토속'은 한 지역 사람들의 생활에 뿌리내린 소박한 풍습에 가까워요. '토속적'으로도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is mostly placed before another noun, as in '토속 음식' or '토속 신앙'. While '전통' covers anything handed down over time, '토속' leans toward simple customs rooted in the daily life of a particular area. It is also often used as '토속적'.

examples.ko: 이 집 된장찌개는 맛이 아주 토속적이에요.
examples.en: This place's soybean paste stew has a very rustic, local taste.

examples.ko: 토속적인 소재로 우리 정서를 표현한 연극이에요.
examples.en: It's a play that expresses our sentiment through folk subject matter.
That singer's songs have a folksy feel.
It's a hanok that keeps its rustic charm.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 토속적인 사투리를 많이 써서 재미있어요.
examples.en: That movie uses a lot of earthy dialect, so it's fun.
I hope the interior isn't too folksy.

explain: '토속적인 맛', '토속적이다'처럼 '-인'이나 '이다'와 함께 자주 써요. 소박하고 그 고장 냄새가 나는 좋은 느낌으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 비슷하게 '향토적'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is often used as '토속적인 맛' or '토속적이다', with '-인' or '이다'. It often carries a pleasant sense of simple, homegrown local flavor. You can also say '향토적' in a similar way.

examples.en: The baby has plumped up nicely.

examples.ko: 토실토실 자란 밤을 한 바구니 주웠어요.
examples.en: I picked up a basket of plump chestnuts.
The puppy grew up chubby and cute.
It's autumn, so the sweet potatoes have ripened plump and well.

examples.ko: 토실토실 살찐 아기 볼을 만져 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to touch the baby's plump cheeks.
These are plump tomatoes ripened in the sun.

explain: 보기 좋게 살이 오른 모양을 말하고, 아기나 귀여운 동물, 알이 찬 열매에 잘 어울려요. '통통'과 비슷하지만 더 건강하고 귀여운 느낌이에요. 어른에게 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a pleasantly filled-out look and suits babies, cute animals, and full, ripe produce. It is similar to '통통' but feels healthier and cuter. Using it for an adult can be rude.

examples.en: The baby's arms are plump.
Lots of plump chestnuts grew on the tree.
The puppy's cheeks are chubby, so it's cute.
These are chicks that have grown plump.
My nephew's hands are chubby and warm.
The sweet potatoes are plump, so they'll probably be tasty.

explain: 살이 보기 좋게 올라 통통하다는 뜻이고, 귀엽고 건강한 느낌이라 아기나 동물, 알이 찬 열매에 써요. '살찌다'는 단순히 체중이 늘 때 쓰고, '토실토실하다'는 칭찬하는 말투예요. 사람의 몸을 두고 어른에게 말하면 조심해야 해요.
explain_en: It describes a pleasantly filled-out look, with a cute and healthy feel, so it is used for babies, animals, and full ripe fruit. '살찌다' simply means gaining weight, while '토실토실하다' is a warm, complimentary tone. Be careful about saying it about an adult's body.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 토질이 좋아서 농사가 잘돼요.
examples.en: The soil here is good, so farming goes well.
If the soil is poor, it's hard to build.
The taste of grapes changes depending on the soil.
Before building a house, we first test the soil.
You have to plant crops that suit the soil.

examples.ko: 이 섬은 토질이 메말라서 채소가 잘 안 자라요.
examples.en: The soil on this island is dry, so vegetables don't grow well.

explain: '토질이 좋다/나쁘다'처럼 땅의 성질을 평가할 때 써요. '흙'이 그냥 흙 자체라면 '토질'은 농사나 건축에서 그 흙이 어떤지를 말하는 느낌이에요. 일상보다는 농사, 공사, 뉴스에서 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is used to evaluate the nature of land, as in '토질이 좋다/나쁘다'. Where '흙' is just soil itself, '토질' is about what that soil is like for farming or building. You hear it more in farming, construction, and the news than in daily chat.

examples.ko: 외래 종교가 이 나라에서 토착화 과정을 거쳤어요.
examples.en: The foreign religion went through a process of localization in this country.
It takes time for a new system to take root.

examples.ko: 커피 문화의 토착화가 빠르게 진행되고 있어요.
examples.en: The localization of coffee culture is progressing fast.
The settling in of alien species affects the ecosystem.
Food also changes in taste once it becomes localized.
I gave a presentation on the localization of Christianity.

explain: 밖에서 들어온 문화, 종교, 제도, 생물이 그곳에 자리 잡아 그 땅의 것이 되는 과정을 말해요. 뉴스나 발표에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '자리를 잡다'라고 많이 해요. 회사가 상품을 현지에 맞게 바꾸는 건 '현지화'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the process in which something from outside, such as a culture, religion, system, or species, settles in and becomes part of the place. It is a word for news and presentations; in daily talk people often say '자리를 잡다'. When a company adapts a product to a local market, people say '현지화'.

examples.en: Foreign culture takes root in our daily life.
This plant has fully become established in Korea.

examples.ko: 햄버거도 현지 입맛에 맞게 토착화하고 있어요.
examples.en: Even hamburgers are being adapted to local tastes.
For a new system to take root, it needs time.
There are really many loanwords that have become naturalized.

examples.ko: 그 종교는 오랜 세월 동안 토착화했어요.
examples.en: That religion became localized over many years.

explain: 주어가 들어온 문화, 제도, 종교, 식물 같은 '밖에서 온 것'이에요. 일상에서는 '자리를 잡다', '뿌리내리다'라고 더 쉽게 말해요. 글이나 발표에서 주로 쓰는 말투예요.
explain_en: The subject is something that came from outside, such as a culture, system, religion, or plant. In daily talk people say it more simply as '자리를 잡다' or '뿌리내리다'. It is mostly a written or presentation-style word.

examples.en: I laid sawdust in the hamster's cage.
When you saw wood, a lot of sawdust comes out.
Sawdust is blowing around on the floor, so I have to clean.
In winter we stay warm with a sawdust stove.
Sawdust piled up high on the floor of the carpentry shop.
Sawdust is also used for growing mushrooms.

explain: 톱질할 때 나오는 나무 가루예요. 대패질할 때 나오는 얇은 조각은 '대팻밥'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 반려동물 바닥재나 난방 연료처럼 쓰임이 꽤 많아요.
explain_en: It is the wood dust that comes out when you saw. The thin shavings from planing are called '대팻밥', which is different. It has several uses, such as bedding for pets or fuel for heating.

examples.en: This accident made me keenly realize the importance of safety.
I deeply feel my fault and sincerely apologize.

examples.ko: 저는 제 실력이 부족하다는 걸 통감해요.
examples.en: I keenly feel that my skills are lacking.
I think everyone should fully recognize their responsibility.

examples.ko: 이번 일로 준비의 중요성을 통감하게 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of this, I came to truly feel the importance of preparation.

examples.ko: 그는 회사를 떠나며 책임을 통감한다고 말했어요.
examples.en: As he left the company, he said he fully felt his responsibility.

explain: '느끼다'보다 훨씬 강하고 격식 있는 말이라 사과문, 뉴스, 연설에서 많이 들려요. 주로 책임, 잘못, 필요성, 부족함처럼 무거운 내용을 마음 깊이 느낄 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '뼈저리게 느끼다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger and more formal than '느끼다', so you hear it in apologies, the news, and speeches. It is used for deeply feeling weighty things such as responsibility, a mistake, a need, or a shortcoming. In everyday talk people also say '뼈저리게 느끼다'.

examples.en: The company gave the employees notice of the contract termination.
The landlord gave notice that we have to leave next month.
We have to notify the contractor of the work stoppage.

examples.ko: 통고받은 업체는 열흘 안에 의견서를 내야 해요.
examples.en: A company that has been notified must submit its written opinion within ten days.

examples.ko: 미리 통고하지 않고 문을 닫으면 어떡해요?
examples.en: What are we supposed to do if you close without notice?
The bank has sent notice that the interest rate is going up.

explain: 상대의 사정과 상관없이 정해진 내용을 공식적으로 알린다는 딱딱한 느낌이에요. 계약, 해지, 처분 같은 공문서나 법적인 상황에서 주로 쓰여요. 요즘 일상에서는 '통보하다'가 더 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It sounds stiff, as if a decision is being officially announced regardless of the other person's situation. It mostly appears in official documents and legal situations like contracts and terminations. In daily life today, '통보하다' is heard more often.

examples.en: The dorm curfew is eleven at night.

examples.ko: 통금 시간 전에 집에 들어가야 해요.
examples.en: I have to get home before curfew.
My parents set a curfew for me.
My home has no curfew, so it's comfortable.

examples.ko: 통금에 걸려서 기숙사 문이 닫혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I got caught by the curfew, and the dorm door was shut.

examples.ko: 예전에는 통금이 있어서 밤에 못 다녔대요.
examples.en: They say that in the past there was a curfew, so people couldn't go out at night.

explain: '통행금지'를 줄인 말이에요. 옛날에는 밤에 다니지 못하게 하던 제도를 가리켰고, 지금은 기숙사나 가족이 정한 귀가 시간을 말할 때 더 많이 써요. 비슷하게 '귀가 시간'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a short form of '통행금지' (traffic ban). It once referred to a system that stopped people from going out at night, and today it is used more for a dorm's or a family's set return-home time. You can also say '귀가 시간'.

examples.en: These sneakers are breathable.
Breathability matters in summer clothes.
Materials with poor breathability make you sweat.
I bought a new, breathable blanket.
This mask lacks breathability, so it feels stuffy.
I chose the hat paying attention to breathability.

explain: 옷, 신발, 이불, 마스크처럼 공기가 잘 통하는 정도를 말할 때 써요. 방이나 건물의 공기가 도는 것은 보통 '환기'나 '통풍'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 물건을 살 때 설명에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes how well air passes through things like clothes, shoes, blankets, and masks. For air circulating in a room or building, people usually say '환기' or '통풍', so they differ. You often see it in product descriptions when shopping.

en: read through; read from cover to cover

examples.en: I read this novel from cover to cover during vacation.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 교과서를 한 번 통독해 보세요.
examples.en: Try reading the textbook all the way through once before the exam.
I read the contract through from start to finish.
I'm attending a group that reads the Bible straight through.

examples.ko: 하루 만에 그 책을 통독했다니 대단해요.
examples.en: Reading that whole book in one day is amazing.
First I read the whole thing through, and then I summarize.

explain: 책이나 문서를 중간에 멈추지 않고 처음부터 끝까지 읽는다는 점이 중요해요. '정독'은 꼼꼼히 천천히 읽는 것이고, '통독'은 전체를 한 번 다 읽는 것이라 서로 달라요. 보통 책 한 권이나 긴 글처럼 큰 덩어리를 목적어로 써요.
explain_en: The key point is reading a book or document from start to finish without stopping. '정독' means reading carefully and slowly, while '통독' means getting through the whole thing once, so they differ. The object is usually a large piece of text such as a whole book.

examples.ko: 그 칼럼은 정부 정책을 통렬하게 비판했어요.
examples.en: That column sharply criticized the government's policy.

examples.ko: 통렬한 풍자가 웃음과 생각을 함께 줘요.
examples.en: The biting satire gives both laughter and food for thought.

examples.ko: 그의 비판은 통렬해서 아무도 반박하지 못했어요.
examples.en: His criticism was so cutting that nobody could rebut it.

examples.ko: 통렬한 반성의 글을 읽고 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: Reading the piece of bitter self-reflection hurt my heart.
This speech is scathing but persuasive.
Everyone went quiet at the cutting remark.

explain: 비판, 풍자, 반성처럼 속을 찌르듯 날카롭고 강한 말이나 글에 써요. 나쁜 뜻이라기보다 '정곡을 찌르는' 느낌이 있어서 칭찬하는 글에도 나와요. 비슷한 '신랄하다'는 말투가 더 매섭고 가혹한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used for sharp, powerful words or writing that cuts to the core, such as criticism, satire, or self-reflection. It is not simply negative, since it carries a sense of hitting the mark, and it can appear even in praise of a piece of writing. The similar '신랄하다' feels harsher and more biting in tone.

examples.en: The child begged me to buy a toy.

examples.ko: 친구에게 한 번만 도와 달라고 통사정했어요.
examples.en: I pleaded with my friend to help me just once.

examples.ko: 선생님께 시험 날짜를 바꿔 달라고 통사정해 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried pleading with the teacher to change the exam date.
No matter how much I begged, they said it wasn't possible.
The way he was pleading was pitiful to see.

examples.ko: 집주인에게 통사정해서 겨우 한 달을 더 살게 됐어요.
examples.en: I pleaded with the landlord and barely got to stay one more month.

explain: 보통 '-아/어 달라고 통사정하다'처럼 간절히 매달리며 부탁하는 상황에 써요. 가볍게 부탁하는 '부탁하다'와 달리 거절당할까 봐 절박하게 비는 느낌이에요. '사정하다'와 비슷하게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is usually used as '-아/어 달라고 통사정하다' for earnestly clinging to someone and asking. Unlike the light '부탁하다', it feels desperate, as if you fear being refused. It is used similarly to '사정하다'.

examples.en: I exchanged names with someone I met for the first time.
Shall we at least introduce ourselves to each other?
I introduced myself to my neighbor and we also exchanged contact numbers.
After exchanging names on the blind date, we had tea.
I ended up exchanging names with the man in the next seat on the train.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 통성명이 끝나자 명함을 주고받았어요.
examples.en: Once the two finished introducing themselves, they exchanged business cards.

explain: 서로 이름을 알려 주며 처음 인사하는 것을 말하고, 'A와/과 통성명하다'처럼 상대와 함께 해요. 조금 격식 있고 예스러운 느낌이라 일상 대화에서는 '인사하다'나 '이름을 묻다'를 더 많이 써요. 처음 만난 사이에서 이름을 주고받는 장면에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It means greeting each other for the first time by telling each other your names, and it is used with a partner, as in 'A와/과 통성명하다'. It sounds a bit formal and old-fashioned, so in daily talk people use '인사하다' or '이름을 묻다' more. It suits scenes where strangers first exchange names.

examples.en: It's a clichéd love story, so the plot is predictable.

examples.ko: 그 드라마는 너무 통속적이어서 보기 싫어요.
examples.en: That drama is so cheap and clichéd that I don't want to watch it.
It's a colloquial expression, so it doesn't fit in a paper.
It's a common-sounding song, but people like it.

examples.ko: 내용이 통속적이라고 해서 가치가 없는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Just because the content is popular and commonplace doesn't mean it has no value.

examples.ko: 통속적으로 그렇게 부르지만 정확한 말은 아니에요.
examples.en: People commonly call it that, but it's not the exact term.

explain: 흔하고 대중적이라는 뜻인데, 예술이나 이야기에는 '뻔하고 수준이 높지 않다'는 부정적인 느낌이 자주 들어가요. 좋게 '대중적이다'라고 말하고 싶을 때는 보통 '대중적'을 써요. '통속적인', '통속적이다', '통속적으로'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: It means common and popular, but when applied to art or stories it often carries a negative feeling of being predictable or low-brow. To praise something as popular, people usually use '대중적' instead. It is used in forms like '통속적인', '통속적이다', and '통속적으로'.

examples.en: The team leader directs a team of ten people.

examples.ko: 팀장이 팀원들을 잘 통솔하면 위기 때도 팀이 흔들리지 않아요.
examples.en: If the team leader leads the team well, the team doesn't waver even in a crisis.

examples.ko: 군대에서는 지휘관이 부대를 잘 통솔하는 것이 가장 중요하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the most important thing in the military is for the commander to lead the unit well.

examples.ko: 많은 사람을 통솔하는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Leading a large group of people is not easy.
We need someone to take charge of the children at camp.
He wasn't able to lead his subordinates well.

explain: 여러 사람을 하나로 모아 이끈다는 뜻으로, '이끌다'보다 격식 있고 권위가 느껴져요. 학급, 팀, 군대 같은 집단을 대상으로 하고, '통솔력'이라는 말을 특히 많이 써요. 한 사람을 가르치거나 돕는 상황에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: It means gathering many people together and leading them as one, and it feels more formal and authoritative than '이끌다'. Its object is a group such as a class, team, or army, and the word '통솔력' (leadership) is especially common. It does not fit situations of teaching or helping a single person.

en: outpatient visit; commuting to a hospital for treatment

examples.ko: 퇴원한 뒤에도 통원 치료를 계속 받아요.
examples.en: Even after being discharged, I keep getting outpatient treatment.

examples.ko: 통원 치료라서 매일 병원에 가야 해요.
examples.en: It's outpatient treatment, so I have to go to the hospital every day.
Does insurance cover outpatient treatment costs too?

examples.ko: 입원은 필요 없고 통원으로 치료할 수 있대요.
examples.en: They say I don't need to be admitted and can be treated as an outpatient.

examples.ko: 할머니는 통원 진료를 받으러 한 달에 두 번 가세요.
examples.en: My grandmother goes twice a month for outpatient visits.

examples.ko: 통원이 힘든 환자는 방문 진료를 신청해요.
examples.en: Patients who find it hard to go to the hospital apply for home visits.

explain: 입원하지 않고 집에서 병원에 다니며 치료받는 것을 말해서 '입원'과 짝이 되는 말이에요. 거의 '통원 치료'나 '통원 진료'처럼 붙여서 쓰고, 보험이나 병원 안내문에 자주 나와요. 보통 '통원 치료를 받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means going to the hospital for treatment from home without being admitted, so it pairs with '입원'. It is almost always used in combinations like '통원 치료' or '통원 진료', and shows up often in insurance and hospital notices. The usual phrase is '통원 치료를 받다'.
